Even coordinates use sine and odd coordinates use cosine at geometrically spaced inverse frequencies. Compute an outer product of positions and frequencies rather than a loop over tokens. Odd model widths need one fewer cosine column. The offset argument supports incremental generation. These encodings are added to token embeddings; unlike RoPE, they are not rotations of projected queries and keys.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** The original frequencies are $PE(p,2i)=\sin(p/10000^{2i/D})$ and $PE(p,2i+1)=\cos(p/10000^{2i/D})$. For any fixed displacement, sine/cosine addition formulas express the shifted pair as a linear transformation of the original pair. This supplies a relative-shift structure without learning a separate vector for every position. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://kazemnejad.com/blog/transformer_architecture_positional_encoding/) and [2](https://huggingface.co/blog/designing-positional-encoding).
